answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to a unique domain. Admission needs proof of control: the agent signs a DNS record under its domain, which the ledger's oracle verifies, so one name mints one identity. The scarce resource is the namespace, one name per registrant. A sybil who mints a thousand clones must buy and renew a thousand domains, a linear cost over the reward horizon, so he cannot wander past the honest set for free. Clones streak like a comet over an ocean of names, yet each rents its own; this blocks cheap mass minting, not a rich attacker.
